## Layouts and ranks: block, rank and panel (`distribute`) {#sec-ch13-layouts}

### Summary

A layout says where each block of a run sits and which blocks are its neighbours. Every exchange, every seam and
every same-process meeting of this chapter asks the layout one of three questions: the location of a block, the
rank at a location, and the neighbour across a face or corner. The `distribute:` card is the layout's only input,
and the layout is the one home of its options, including how many blocks one process runs.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Map a block rank to a location $(r_x, r_y, f)$, where $f$ is the cubed-sphere panel (0 elsewhere),
map a location back to a rank, and give the neighbour rank at an offset $(\iota_3, \iota_2, \iota_1)$.

**Data.** In: the `distribute:` card. Out: integer ranks and locations; no field data.

**Placement.** At construction; read by every exchange (@sec-ch13-ghost) and seam (@sec-ch03).

**Activation.** `distribute: layout` (`slab`, `cubed` or `cubed-sphere`; default `slab`), `nb1`, `nb2`, `nb3`
(default 1 each) and `blocks_per_process` (default 1).

**Guarantee / limits.** The map is a bijection on the ranks of the run; edge neighbours are symmetric. No
physics depends on it beyond which block sits where.

**Evidence.** @sec-ch13-layouts-tests.
:::

On the cubed sphere a run has $6\,n_b^2$ blocks, $n_b$ along each panel edge (`nb2` = `nb3` = $n_b$). A process
owns `blocks_per_process` consecutive ranks; the owning process and the block's index within it are the quotient
and remainder of the rank by `blocks_per_process`. The panel of a block is the third component of its location
(`panel_of`), and `is_cubed_sphere` is a property of the layout options, not of the layout object.

### Derivation

There is no equation: the layout is a map. Its properties are stated here and checked by a run. For every
$n_b \in \{1,2,3,4\}$ the cubed-sphere layout has $6\,n_b^2$ ranks (6, 24, 54, 96) on panels 0 to 5;
`rank_of(loc_of(r))` is `r` for every rank and `loc_of` returns $(-1,-1,-1)$ one past the last; each of the four
edge neighbours of a rank is another valid rank, and the edge relation is symmetric (a block is an edge
neighbour of each of its edge neighbours); every corner neighbour is a valid rank.[^lay-run] The process map is
$p = \lfloor r / B \rfloor$, $\ell = r \bmod B$ for rank $r$ and $B$ = `blocks_per_process`
(`owner_process_rank`, `local_block_index`), whose inverse is $r = pB + \ell$ (`global_block_rank`).

[^lay-run]: [sha: 1b12ea5dc7eb71c89f07256d10cf379c20defe20] `a2run/ch13/cs_neighbors.py` in the writer's workspace,
    through the snapy Python bindings (`CubedSphereLayout`); this build's `src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp`,
    `layout.hpp` and `src/options/layout.yaml` have no diff to the pin. Not an executable check of section 7: it
    imports snapy.

### Numerical method

The slab and cubed layouts number blocks in Morton (Z) order over the block grid; the cubed-sphere layout numbers
each panel the same way and the panels in turn. A neighbour across one edge is one step of `_step_one`, which
crosses to the adjacent panel when the step leaves the panel. A corner neighbour is two such steps, $x_2$ first
when that step stays on the panel, else $x_3$ first; where both steps would cross an edge (a cube corner) the
layout returns the block one step away along $x_2$. @fig-ch13-layouts shows the order and the panel net.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch13-layouts
#| fig-cap: "(a) Rank order of a $4\\times4$ block grid: Morton (Z) order. (b) The cubed-sphere panel numbering $0$ to $5$ as an unfolded net."
#| fig-alt: "Left, a four by four grid of numbered squares joined by a Z-shaped curve; right, the cross-shaped net of the cube with face numbers."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.figures.fig_layouts_morton import make_fig
make_fig()
```

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| options (the `distribute:` card) | {{< code src/options/layout.yaml >}} | `blocks_per_process` | `distribute` |
| option struct | {{< code src/layout/layout.hpp LayoutOptionsImpl >}} | `LayoutOptionsImpl` | `layout`, `nb1`-`nb3` |

| index in its process | {{< code src/layout/layout.hpp LayoutOptionsImpl::local_block_index >}} | `local_block_index` | `blocks_per_process` |
| layout type | {{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::create >}} | `create` | `layout` |
| rank to location | {{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::loc_of >}} | `loc_of` | none |
| location to rank | {{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::rank_of >}} | `rank_of` | none |
| neighbour at an offset | {{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::neighbor_rank >}} | `neighbor_rank` | none |
| panel of a rank | {{< code src/layout/layout.hpp LayoutImpl::panel_of >}} | `panel_of` | none |

`LayoutImpl::create` builds the layout named by `layout`; an unknown name is refused there. The process of a
block and its index in the process are read wherever a same-process path is chosen (`is_local_block`).

The map properties of the Derivation are from a run, not a ctest (@sec-ch13-layouts). Neither test was run at the
pin for this chapter (missing evidence); both are CPU tests.

### Limits

The schema's own description of `layout` names `slab` and `cubed-sphere` only, while `create` also accepts
`cubed`. At a cube corner the corner neighbour is a convention (one step along $x_2$), not a geometric
neighbour; @sec-ch03 covers how corner ghosts are filled. Switch combinations are in @sec-ch12-matrix.
